ideas.truth: We've learned to expect that tech takes more than it gives — so the rare moment something gives back feels almost startling.
ideas.moment: The instant a single key turns and, instead of just opening a door, floods the room with more light than the gap should allow.
ideas.key_frame: A brass key mid-turn in an antique lock, warm light beginning to spill past the edges of the door.

ideas.truth: People trust a deal more when the extra bit feels unprompted, not advertised.
ideas.moment: A hand turns a key in a piggy-bank slot; the expected coins fall, then one more rolls out on its own, unbidden.
ideas.key_frame: Close-up of a coin rolling free of the pile, catching light as it goes.

ideas.truth: The best kind of generosity is quiet — it doesn't need a person in frame to be felt.
ideas.moment: A vending-style key turns in a simple metal drawer; it opens on a single item, and a second smaller one slides out after, unasked for.
ideas.key_frame: A metal drawer creeping open, one item sitting inside plus a small extra tucked beside it.

why: It makes the wordplay on 'key' literal and premium rather than gimmicky, needs no human likeness to stay consistent, and the 'more light than the gap allows' image is a clean, ownable visual metaphor for 'a little more.'
treatment: In near-total darkness, a single ornate brass key rests beside a tall antique wooden door, lit by one warm spotlight. Camera pushes in slowly. An unseen hand lifts the key and turns it — a metallic scrape, a click. The door begins to open, and light doesn't just enter the gap, it spills past it, wider and warmer than it should be, dust catching in the beam. Camera eases back to take it in. A hushed voice says the line as the glow settles into a steady, generous light. The wordmark and tagline hold on the final frame. No faces, no set dressing beyond the key, the door, and the dark — just quiet cinematic proof that a little more was given than was asked.

scenes.prompt: Slow, deliberate dolly-in toward the key. An unseen hand enters from the bottom of frame, grips the key, and turns it clockwise in one smooth continuous motion until it clicks fully into place. Ambient hush and a low resonant hum underneath; a soft metallic scrape as the key turns, resolving into a single clear click. No dialogue.
scenes.first_frame_still_prompt: The same ornate brass skeleton key with a looping head, resting beside a tall antique wooden door set into a dark stone wall, lit by one warm overhead spotlight, cinematic and premium in mood. Extreme close framing on the key, the door softly out of focus behind it, shallow depth of field, fine film grain, near-black negative space around the light pool.

scenes.prompt: Camera holds, then drifts back half a step as the door begins to open on the click from the key. Warm golden light spills out through the widening gap, but visibly wider and brighter than the gap itself, drifting dust motes catching in the beam and drifting past the frame edges. A soft rising chime swells under a hushed, unhurried spoken line: 'One key to AI that always gives back a little more.' By the final beat the light has settled into a steady, gentle glow.
scenes.spoken: One key to AI that always gives back a little more.

finish.music: Yes — a single sustained warm swell, minimal and reverberant, like one held piano note with soft strings underneath; quiet confidence, not triumphant.
